$comment: Held-out evaluation labels (scripts/eval.py). knownPositives come from a code audit by an AI agent (Claude) that read only the project's source at the pinned revision: it did not run Midwrite and did not see its output. findings are classified afterwards, finding by finding, with the Phase 2 classes. No independent human review has been performed; an AI agent checking another AI agent's results is not independent human validation. Corrections go in `corrections` with a reason, never by editing a label to raise a score.

knownPositives.scope: unhandled half-written-state windows in server code; the audit was capped at 30 entries, highest confidence first, so the list is a sample when the project has more

findings.by: AI agent (Claude), finding-by-finding source review, separate from the auditor; did not see knownPositives

knownPositives.consequence: The thread moves from INBOX to SNOOZED in Gmail but no wake-at key is written, so it is never unsnoozed.
The connection row is gone but its chat history and R2 attachments are orphaned; nothing can find them again.
If the delete fails after the cancel, the account still exists with its Autumn subscriptions cancelled, and nothing restores them.
User and connection rows are deleted while per-mailbox chat history and R2 attachments are orphaned for good.
OAuth tokens are revoked at the provider but, if the delete never commits, connection rows keep dead tokens that look valid.
Tokens nulled while the IMAP status still says active; settings report an active connection that needs a reconnect.

knownPositives.firstEffect: refreshAccessToken(...) (may rotate the refresh token) at line 230
knownPositives.consequence: A rotated refresh token is kept only in memory when the persist fails (only logged); after eviction the old token yields invalid_grant.

knownPositives.firstEffect: executeMailTool(...) (Gmail send / draft save) at line 253
knownPositives.consequence: Mail is sent but the action stays running without its result, or is marked failed by the catch although the mail went out.
The stale wake-at key survives and the cron later re-adds INBOX to threads the user has since archived.
If the queue send throws, the hook fails after the campaign was sent and the retried login sends the whole campaign again.

findings.notes: auth.ts:213-225 Autumn cancel is try/catch log-only and the revokes (227-250) run under Promise.allSettled: deliberate best-effort steps of account deletion.

auth.ts:242 revokeToken runs in Promise.allSettled with log-only failures, and clearMailboxChatData (chat-attachments.ts:206-215) is documented 'Never throws': explicitly best-effort around db.deleteUser.
parseFileToMarkdown (context-dev.ts:53-73) is a stateless conversion POST; it leaves no external state to be inconsistent with the later R2 put (chat-attachments.ts:77).

A failed R2 put (chat-attachments.ts:76-86) makes storeAttachment throw before its URL is returned; sweepOrphanedAttachments (:180-191) deletes unreferenced objects and a missing .md is handled (:127-128).
The first fetch is the OAuth token exchange in getAccessToken (google-subscription.factory.ts:70-87); it changes no external state the request at :97 could leave half-done.
resourceExists (google-subscription.factory.ts:106-111) is a read-only GET, so failing before the topic PUT at :120 leaves nothing partial.
Same pair: resourceExists at google-subscription.factory.ts:107 is a read-only GET before the topic-create PUT at :120.
A topic without its IAM policy (factory :120/:131) is repaired by the idempotent subscribe, which main.ts:1038-1062 re-enqueues while gmail_sub_age (written last, :300) is missing.
As above: topic without IAM converges on the next subscribe_queue run enqueued by the cron (main.ts:1044-1062); steps are idempotent.
getIamPolicy at google-subscription.factory.ts:139 is a read-only GET; only setIamPolicy (:157) writes.
Duplicate pair: getIamPolicy (factory :139) is a read before setIamPolicy (:157).
resourceExists at google-subscription.factory.ts:189 is a GET existence probe before the subscription PUT at :190.
Same pair: the first fetch at google-subscription.factory.ts:189 is read-only.
Stopping between setupPubSubTopic (factory :287) and createPubSubSubscription (:290) leaves gmail_sub_age unwritten (:300), so the cron re-enqueues the idempotent subscribe (main.ts:1038-1062).
A missing gmail_sub_age.put after the subscription (factory :290-303) only makes the cron (main.ts:1040-1061) re-run the idempotent subscribe.
scheduled() unsnooze enqueue (main.ts:1025-1033) and subscribe sends (:1058-1062) are unrelated, recomputed from KV every run, and the unsnooze side is try/catch log-only.
renewMailboxWatch (agent/index.ts:1017-1029): a failed gmail_sub_age.put after the idempotent watchMailbox is caught and retried via mail_watch_renew_at; the cron re-subscribes stale entries.

disconnectImap (agent/index.ts:1862-1877) does two updates without a transaction; once tokens are nulled, runImapSync (:1614-1618) never re-runs it, so connectionImap.status can stay 'active' (low impact: nothing reads it today).
unsnoozeThreadsHandler (agent/index.ts:3519-3525) rethrows on failed KV deletes; the expired keys stay and the cron (main.ts:996-1033) re-runs the idempotent label change and deletes.
assistant.ts:231-232 comment: an indeterminate send is never retried because duplicate mail is worse than an error; the stuck 'running' state is accepted on purpose.
Both calls are read-only GETs (DNS-over-HTTPS lookup at bimi.ts:24 and the logo fetch) in a query procedure.
getByDomain (bimi.ts:178-193) only does a DNS TXT GET and a logo GET; neither is a write.
Unsnooze-on-access (mail.ts:193-198) is try/catch log-only; a leftover expired key is consumed by the cron (main.ts:996-1033).

snoozeThreads applies SNOOZED and removes INBOX (mail.ts:619) before writing the wakeAt KV keys (:622-628); if the put fails the thread stays snoozed forever (cron main.ts:996-1022 never finds it), with no compensation.
If the KV delete fails after the unsnooze label change (mail.ts:642-648), the stale key is consumed by the cron unsnooze path, which repeats the idempotent change.

reviewQueue.issue: the auditor lists this window as unhandled; the finding labeler classified the matching finding(s) as intended-risk. Both are AI judgments; neither label was changed. A human reviewer should decide and record the outcome in `corrections`.
